sections.content: Recursion is a function calling itself to solve smaller versions of the same problem — like Russian nesting dolls.
Every recursive function needs a base case (the simplest possible input) and a recursive case that moves toward it. Missing the base case means infinite recursion and a crash.
Key points: recursion excels at tree-like problems (file systems, JSON), but loops are often simpler for plain repetition.
Summary: Recursion — practice the example by changing values and predicting the output before running it.
